In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chromia is a magnetoelectric antiparallel ferromagnet.
the magnetoelectric coupling in chromia films is strongly suppressed, but not entirely suppressed.
the spin reversal field of chromia can be controlled by the film thickness and the temperature, which makes it a promising candidate for future spintronics applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic reversal field is strongly temperature dependent, and the coercive field is strongly thickness dependent.
we have shown the possibility of magnetic switching in thin films of chromia, and we have demonstrated a giant temperature sensitivity of the switching field.
the magnetic field-induced spin reversal in thin films of the magnetoelectric chromic antiferromagnet can be achieved by a magnetic field alone, without the need for an electric field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetoelectric coupling in thin chromia films is strongly enhanced compared to bulk chromia, thus enabling magnetic field-induced spin switching.
the magnetic field response of chromia is not limited to the bulk, but also applies for thin films.
the magnetic field-induced reversal of the magnetoelectric chromic antiferromagnet is possible for thin enough films and that this reversal field exhibits an unusually large temperature sensitivity.
